assets.statement: All-primes choice makes the a_k sequence finite, violating the canonical premise; vacuous-goodness argument is domain drift, needs an infinite survivor construction plus literal quantifier-order verification.

Graham's covering-prime construction has all covering primes dividing a_1, so N=a_1 shares a factor with every term, violating the canonical universal coprimality condition; repair requires a covering scheme with gcd(a_0,a_1)=1 and no single integer meeting all covering primes.

L1-as-branch-B-evidence fails: Maynard bound is subsequence-only (hidden-subsequence attack) and does not match the quantifier reversal of o(log N) (needs all-N failure at positive density, not infinitely many N); repair = uniform c·log N lower bound on the full primes, an equivalent-strength open p

refuted at smallest parameters: r=2, k=2 family I₁={2,3}, I₂={24,25} gives total product 3600=60², exactly verified; Pell a(a+1)=6t² yields infinitely many length-2 square-product blocks, so k=2 imposes no obstruction and any close must use a fixed r across all k≥2 with explicit integrality.

L1 ("all positive integers are sums of ≤3 2-full numbers") refuted by n=7: powerful ≤7 are {1,4}, 3-term sums miss 7 (also n=15); canonical "large" hedge is load-bearing, so any close needs an explicit threshold/exception set.

Vacuous subset fact, coprimality and both target sums never used; quantifier slip (∃-level fact offered for ∀-level proposition) and circularity confirmed; route R005 has no standing reduction and must produce a genuine bound or separating family.
